causalModel.founding: The Legion built a road stage a short walk from Soulrest. The wreck-salvage families kept the stage when the pay stopped.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: The stage stands on the last firm ground before the track turns inland. The sea lies to the south, out of sight of the stage. Wreckage from the Southern Sea comes ashore on the coast to the south.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: Salvage rights here are hereditary and counted. The stage's walls stand and its yard can be locked. The families store their salvage in the walled yard.
causalModel.pressures: No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries. Two families each claim the keeper's office.
causalModel.wouldChangeIf: A revived road with paid Legion keepers would make Chasepoint a proper town again.

districts.notes: The Imperial stage on the coast track, its walled yard behind it and the old stable where the salvage now dries.

why.what: This district is the Legion's stage and its walled yard. The salvage families keep the stage and yard.
why.whyHere: The Legion put a stage on the last firm ground before the track turns inland.
why.whySpot: The stage stands on the east lip of the plateau. The stage door faces the coast track.
why.whyNeighbours: The coast track runs past the stage door. The families' homes lie south of the yard.
why.playerPurpose: The district holds the station-keeper and the salvage stall. The yard is where the timber is counted.
why.microGeography: The ground is a low plateau about seven metres up. The plateau falls gently east to the track.

districts.notes: Two plank houses of the salvage households on the dry ground south of the yard.

why.what: This district holds the plank houses of the first two salvage households.
why.whyHere: The families live beside the stage they keep.
why.whySpot: The houses stand on the dry south end of the plateau. The houses stand above the swamp.
why.whyNeighbours: The yard lies north of the houses. The coast track runs past on the east.
why.playerPurpose: The households hold the salvage rights. They argue over who keeps the stage.
why.microGeography: The ground is firm on the plateau's south end, seven metres up.

districts.notes: The third salvage household's bamboo hut on the plateau's eastern edge.

why.what: The third salvage household built a bamboo hut in downriver style.
why.whyHere: The third family came late to the salvage rights. The family built what they could carry up.
why.whySpot: The hut stands on the last firm ground east of the home path. The slope to the shore begins beyond the hut.
why.whyNeighbours: The plank houses lie west of the hut. The smokehouse lies north of the hut.
why.playerPurpose: The third household hauls wreck timber up from the shore.
why.microGeography: The hut stands on a low rise on the plateau's eastern edge.

parcels.orientationWhy: The stage door faces east onto the coast track.

playerPurpose.note: The station-keeper's stage and the salvage stall at its door.
Word for the road is left at the stage door; wreck survivors are brought here first.

why.what: This is the Legion's road stage. It has plaster walls under a thatch roof.
why.whyHere: The Legion built it as a stage where travellers change and rest.
why.whySpot: The stage stands on the east lip of the plateau. It stands square to the coast track.
why.whyNeighbours: The salvage stall stands at the stage's north end. The yard wall stands behind the stage.
why.playerPurpose: The station-keeper lives at the stage. The station-keeper sells wreck goods recovered in the past week.
why.microGeography: The ground is firm on the plateau's east edge, above the track.

parcels.worksWithWhy: The drying stable stands 4.5 m inside the yard wall. The yard lock holds in the salvage that dries in the stable.
parcels.orientationWhy: The stable's open front faces east across the yard to the stage.

playerPurpose.note: The timber stacks counted against their ships.

why.what: This is the stage's old stable. Rope and nets hang to dry in it.
why.whyHere: The stable holds no horses now. The families dry salvage cordage under its roof.
why.whySpot: The stable stands inside the yard wall, west of the stage.
why.whyNeighbours: The timber stacks lie south of the stable in the yard.
why.playerPurpose: The families count and stack salvaged rope, nets and timber.
why.microGeography: The ground is level in the middle of the walled yard.

parcels.orientationWhy: The house door faces north to the yard and the stage.

playerPurpose.note: The salvage household that claims the stage-keeper's office.

why.what: This is the plank house of the household that works the shingle shore to the south.
why.whyHere: The household works the shingle shore to the south. The household keeps the yard.
why.whySpot: The house stands on dry ground south of the yard. It stands near the coast track.
why.whyNeighbours: The yard lies north of the house. The second house lies west of it.
why.playerPurpose: The family band lives here. The family band knows the ship behind each salvage lot.
why.microGeography: The ground is firm on the south of the plateau.

parcels.orientationWhy: The house door turns north-east toward the path to the yard.

playerPurpose.note: The household that keeps the tally of the salvage.

why.what: This is a plank house. The household that keeps the count lives here.
why.whyHere: The second household holds the other half of the salvage rights.
why.whySpot: The house stands in the south-west of the plateau, behind the first house.
why.whyNeighbours: The first house lies east of it. The yard lies north of it.
why.playerPurpose: The merchant's household lives here. The household keeps the tally of every lot.
why.microGeography: The ground is firm at the plateau's south-west end.

parcels.orientationWhy: The wall closes the yard on its north and west sides. The stage closes the yard on the east.

why.what: This is the dry-stone wall round the stage's yard.
why.whyHere: An Imperial stage walls its yard. The wall lets the keepers lock the yard.
why.whySpot: The wall runs along the west side of the yard. It meets the north run at the corner.
why.whyNeighbours: The stage closes the east side of the yard.
why.playerPurpose: The wall marks the yard where the salvage is kept.
why.microGeography: The wall follows the level top of the plateau round the yard.

parcels.orientationWhy: The hut door turns north-west toward the home path and the stage.

playerPurpose.note: The household that hauls the wreck timber up from the shore.

why.what: This is a small bamboo hut. The third salvage household lives in it.
why.whyHere: The third family holds the last share of the salvage rights.
why.whySpot: The hut stands east of the home path. It stands on the last firm ground before the slope to the shore.
why.whyNeighbours: The first house lies west of the hut across the path. The smokehouse lies north of the hut.
why.playerPurpose: The player meets the newest salvage family here, the one with the smallest share.
why.microGeography: The hut floor sits a step above the home path, on dry ground clear of the shore damp.

parcels.orientationWhy: The loft door turns south-west onto the path from the homes.

playerPurpose.note: The families' store of dry salvage cordage.

why.what: This is a plank net loft. The families store dry nets and rope in it.
why.whyHere: The families dry cordage in the yard stable. They keep the cordage in the loft once it is dry.
why.whySpot: The loft stands just west of the yard wall. The yard wall stands between the loft and the wet wind off the sea.
why.whyNeighbours: The yard wall lies east of the loft. The second house lies south of the loft.
why.playerPurpose: The loft is the families' store of the salvage cordage they sell.
why.microGeography: The ground is level at the foot of the yard wall.

parcels.orientationWhy: The smokehouse's open front faces north-west to the stage path.

why.what: This is a second old stable, open on one side. The households now use it to smoke fish.
why.whyHere: The households smoke their catch. They sell the smoked catch with the salvage.
why.whySpot: The smokehouse stands on the coast track north of the brazier. It stands downwind of the houses.
why.whyNeighbours: The stage lies west of the smokehouse. The third house lies south of the smokehouse.
why.playerPurpose: The merchant sells the smoked fish at the stall.
why.microGeography: The ground beside the coast track is firm and well-drained.

routes.why: Carts and walkers leave the main road here. The path runs west past the stall to the stage door and its yard.
This route runs from the coast track south to the first house.
This route runs from the home path into the yard from the south. It passes the timber on the way to the stable.
The tally merchant walks from the yard path to the second house. The merchant carries the day's count.
The third household leaves the home path here. The path leads to the household's own door.
The families carry dry nets from the homes round the yard wall. The nets go to the loft.
The households carry the catch from the track straight to the smokehouse.

questSockets.why: The timber stacks stand in the yard. The families count each lot against its ship.
Travellers on the coast track stop at the stage door first. Word for the road is left at the stage door.
The families cry wreck salvage at the stage. Survivors and caged animals taken off a wreck are brought to the stage first.

occupants.cultureRole: station-keeper who holds an inherited Imperial office

approaches.sequence: A traveller comes down the coast track. The stage's straight ridge shows over the scrub, and so does the square yard wall. The post at the bend stands beside the track.
approaches.wayfinding: The stage door faces the track. The path to the homes leaves the track south of the stage.

networkTerminals.why: South of the stage the old coast track runs on to the houses. The households use it as their own way. People walk it on foot. It has no gate.

combatSpaces.why: The walled yard lies between the stage and the old stable. The yard is level and open.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: The lore source is the catalogue record Chasepoint (road-station-village, M2). The record covers the stage, its station-keeper and the salvage households.
scaleGrounding.why: Three salvage households and the station-keeper live at Chasepoint. Chasepoint has three plank houses and the stage. It also has a net loft. The households dry their cordage in one old stable. A second old stable is their smokehouse.

candidates.why: The dry plateau top lies west of the track. It has room for the stage square to the track. It also has room for a walled yard behind the stage and for the houses south of the stage.
The plotted anchor lies on the track itself.
candidates.rejectedBecause: The anchor stands on the track's east lip. The ground there falls two metres to the province road. There is no level room for a yard.
